notes: The runs array contains one run for each eval/configuration pair (8 runs total); the reported standard deviations therefore describe differences across the four evals, not repeat-run stability or flakiness.

Timing was unavailable for this benchmark. Every time_seconds value is recorded as 0.0, so those values are placeholders and must not be interpreted as zero execution time or as a measured timing delta between configurations.

Every run records tool_calls=0 and errors=0. The assertion results therefore measure the written intended workflows and their treatment of unavailable runtime evidence, not observed public-tool execution.

Exact capability preflight differentiates the configurations in evals 1 and 3: with_skill passes and without_skill fails. Eval 2's preflight assertion passes in both configurations, while eval 4's exact five-capability preflight assertion fails in both; the with_skill run names only animation.temporal and output.sprite_atlas, whereas the baseline supplies no exact capability ledger.

All four eval 1 assertions covering inspected values, exact apply_operations shape, expectedRevisionId binding, and compare_revisions pass with_skill and fail without_skill. The baseline uses guessed operations and non-contract field names, while the skill-guided output keeps response-derived values unresolved and shows the required dry-run/replay sequence.

Visual and artifact review requirements separate the configurations on the supported workflows: the with_skill runs pass the full 3D/contact-sheet/native-frame assertions in evals 1 and 2, while both baseline runs fail them; eval 2 also passes audit-only artifact verification with_skill and fails it without_skill.

For unsupported requests, both configurations preserve several safety boundaries: eval 3 stops before mutation and avoids approximation or bypasses, and eval 4 stops before mutation and avoids manufactured animation or hidden routes. The with_skill advantage is concentrated in explicit unsupported-capability classification, named prerequisites, directional-versus-temporal distinctions, and future handoff evidence.

The no-source-read/no-canonical-JSON/no-direct-file-or-post-processing assertion passes in both configurations in all four evals. These safety assertions confirm a shared boundary but do not differentiate skill value in this benchmark.

Token counts are higher with_skill in every eval, not just in the aggregate. The smallest relative increase is eval 2 (8111 versus 5980, about 1.36x), and the largest is eval 3 (6211 versus 1508, about 4.12x).

Eval 4 is the only with_skill run below a perfect pass rate (7/8) because of the incomplete exact capability preflight. Without_skill varies from 1/8 in eval 1 to 4/7 in eval 3, but with only one run per eval/configuration these differences cannot establish repeat-run consistency.
